'''''Arisaema''''' is a large and diverse [[genus]] of the [[flowering plant]] family [[Araceae]]. The largest concentration of species is in China and Japan, with other species [[native plant|native]] to other parts of southern Asia as well as eastern and central Africa, Mexico and eastern North America.<ref name=9i9i9i9i9i99i9i>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=15221 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>  Asiatic species are often called '''cobra lilies''', while western species are often called '''jack-in-the-pulpit'''; both names refer to the distinctive appearance of the flower, which consists of an erect central [[spadix (botany)|spadix]] rising from a [[bract|spathe]].<ref>Govaerts, R. & Frodin, D.G. (2002). World Checklist and Bibliography of Araceae (and Acoraceae): 1-560. The Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=102590 Flora China Vol. 23 Page 43, <big>天南星属</big> tian nan xing shu, ''Arisaema'' Martius, Flora. 14: 459. 1831. ]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=102590 Flora of North America, Vol. 22, ''Arisaema'' Martius, Flora. 14: 459. 1831.]</ref>

==Classification and relationships==
The closest relatives of ''Arisaema'' appear to be ''[[Pinellia]]'' and ''[[Typhonium]]'' (although the latter as defined in 2004 seems to be [[paraphyletic]], having given rise to ''Arisaema'' and other genera).<ref name="renner">{{citation | doi = 10.3732/ajb.91.6.881 | title = A chloroplast phylogeny of Arisaema (Araceae) illustrates Tertiary floristic links between Asia, North America, and East Africa | year = 2004 | author = Renner, S. S. | journal = American Journal of Botany | volume = 91 | issue = 6 | pages = 881–8 | last2 = Zhang | first2 = L.-B. | last3 = Murata | first3 = J. | pmid=21653444| url = http://nbn-resolving.de/urn:nbn:de:bvb:19-epub-14634-6 | url-access = subscription }}</ref> One unusual trait shared by all ''Arisaema'' species, and not those of other genera, is [[sequential hermaphroditism]]. ''Arisaema'' plants are typically male when small, and female or hermaphroditic when large, with a single plant capable of changing sex based on nutrition<ref name="renner"/> and genetics,<ref>{{citation | doi = 10.3732/ajb.90.12.1729 | title = Local differentiation and plasticity in size and sex expression in jack-in-the-pulpit, Arisaema triphyllum (Araceae) | year = 2003 | author = Vitt, P. | journal = American Journal of Botany | volume = 90 | issue = 12 | pages = 1729–35 | last2 = Holsinger | first2 = K. E. | last3 = Jones | first3 = C. S. | pmid=21653349| doi-access = free }}</ref> and perhaps changing sex several times during its long life (20 years or more).<ref name="renner"/>

===Sections===
A phylogenetic study in 2016 by Ohi-toma et al. recognized 15 sections in the genus.<ref name="Ohi-Toma Wu Murata Murata pp. 100–114">{{cite journal | last1=Ohi-Toma | first1=Tetsuo | last2=Wu | first2=Sugong | last3=Murata | first3=Hiroko | last4=Murata | first4=Jin | title=An updated genus-wide phylogenetic analysis of ''Arisaema'' (Araceae) with reference to sections | journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=182 | issue=1 | date=2016-06-30 | issn=0024-4074 | doi=10.1111/boj.12459 | pages=100–114| doi-access=free }}</ref>
